what: How much does code layout alone move this benchmark?
host: Ryzen 7 5800X, 6 threads, Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0, 247-token prompt, 32 tokens
why: Moving the embedding gather into the backend measured -8% prefill twice, while the gather itself measures 0.0014 ms and the logits are byte-identical
method: Builds that behave identically, compared with tools/ab_runner.py at 15 pairs each against one reference build. The probes add an unused member function to the baseline and change nothing else.

pure_layout_probes.build: baseline + unused function (copy of the removed one)
pure_layout_probes.note: trips the advance rule with no behaviour change

embed_variants.build: plus the removed function as dead code
gather call forced out of line
prefill body forced out of line
token id in a member slot instead of a local

findings: Code layout alone spans about four points of prefill on this cell, wider than the runner's 3% band.
A binary with one unused function added and no behaviour change failed the advance rule on decode at 12 of 15 pairs.
The -8% build is outside the layout band, so it was a genuinely poor layout rather than noise; adding one local to a very large inline body was enough to cause it.
Forcing functions out of line made it worse, not better. Moving the local into a member slot restored it.
consequences: A single-build A/B cannot gate a few-percent change on this cell. A candidate should be compared against several perturbed builds of the same behaviour, not one.
Earlier few-percent prefill conclusions on this model carry this uncertainty; the 0.6B prefill cell also failed its own A/A at -3.53% earlier.
limits: One machine, one compiler (MSVC 14.50), one model and prompt. Says nothing about GCC or Clang layouts.
